text: rwb-reporting builds the queue, ageing and breach measures from the events into its own projection (CaseTransferred, CaseAllocated, CaseStateChanged, TimerBreached and the decision record), and rwb-case publishes no measure feed and writes no file; the nightly lake copy of JOB-15 and the INT-19 and INT-20 outbound batch are removed under DP-17.
why: The legacy publication of the measure snapshot was the JOB-15 copy to the data lake for Power BI, and Arch v5 removes the data lake and both interfaces, so the story needs one stated replacement for the published measures of REQ-RDF-012.
read: RWB-E1-030 sections 3, 4 step 9 and 12; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 8 ('Data lake / Power BI not connected (INT-19/20 removed)'); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-reporting owner at the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1030-CON and in the wave 1 verification loop.
impact: If reporting needs a published measure read instead of a projection, one operation is added to RWB-P3-E1030-CON and one controller to RWB-P3-E1030-APP; the snapshot table, its status and the reconciliation rule do not change.

text: MSG-P3-028, MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-029 are delivered at wave 1 on the ACE notification path with their message ID as the template key, as the monolith did, and move to rwb-comms when P6 lands; the story consumes no contract of a notice service.
why: The legacy notifier sent the three messages through the monolith's notification path and no source assigns a notice contract to this key, so the alert rows of section 14 need one stated delivery path that adds no contract dependency.
read: RWB-E1-030 section 4 steps 4, 7 and 10 and section 14; FSD P3 v4 'Existing capability check' row 'Notification path | REUSE | ACE notification path'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 10
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-comms owner and the platform notification owner before the story's Done.
impact: If the messages move to rwb-comms at wave 1, one consumed contract row and one adapter appear in RWB-P3-E1030-APP and the C dependency is added; no AC, no message text and no snapshot field changes.

text: The run record of a business date is the Temporal record of the DailyCaseRun run (its activity results name the moves and any case that stayed with MSG-P7-003), and the legacy rerun call is replaced by triggering the Schedule rwb-case-rebalance-daily by hand under Platform administration U, with no REST operation published; a consumer reads a date's moves through GET /cases with the queue filter and the snapshot through GET /queues.
why: The legacy job table, the job monitor and the rerun endpoint were Quartz artifacts of the monolith; the Schedule replaces the job trigger and the ownership map publishes no jobs or run-record operation, so the run record and the rerun surface need one stated default.
read: RWB-E1-030 sections 4 step 1, 5 (X4) and 12 (job table and rerun endpoint); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-06; _work/msr/context/P3.md REST rows; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10
confirm: Solution architect with the workflow platform owner and the RW-PLATADM owner before the story's Done.
impact: If a published run record or rerun operation is required, one operation and one table row appear in the contract and one controller in the build story; the moves, the snapshot and the ACs do not change.

text: The Schedule fires at 06:30 in the bank's business time zone held as a value in the values file (assumed Asia/Bangkok until the business owner confirms it), with an overlap policy of skip and a catch-up window held as a value; replica counts, resource limits, the ingress host, the alert thresholds and the activity retry values are values in the same file with no default chosen by this story.
why: The chart and the Schedule must be renderable in SIT and UAT, and no source gives a zone, a catch-up window, a replica count or an alert threshold, so the story needs one stated set of value names without inventing the numbers.
read: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-06 (Daily 06:30); RWB-E1-030 section 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 44; Template and Rules R1 U7 (dates and times copied, values not invented)
confirm: DevOps lead with the business owner and the workflow platform team at the SIT dry run.
impact: If the zone or the catch-up window differs, one values key changes per environment and the runbook state table changes; no code, no schema and no AC changes.
